interface.name: denial_insets_manager_v1
interface.description:
Denial's mobile shell reserves space for system bars in ordinary app windows. A client which already supplies those insets to its application may opt out per wl_surface. This does not change the surface's role, buffer coordinates, scale, synchronization, or input semantics. Desktop layout is unaffected. This protocol does not communicate inset dimensions; declaring a surface requires the client to know and apply the appropriate system insets itself.
Since version 2 a client may also lay a surface out around the on-screen keyboard instead of having the shell move it; see get_keyboard_inset. The two declarations are independent.

entry.name: mapped_surface
entry.summary: the surface already has a committed buffer

entry.name: keyboard_inset_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a keyboard inset object

request.name: set_self_managed

description.summary: the application already handles system insets

request.description: Declare that the client handles system insets for this surface. Send this before the initial buffer commit (normally before the initial xdg_surface configure), or while the surface is unmapped. The request takes effect immediately and is idempotent. The declaration lasts for the wl_surface lifetime, including unmap/remap, and is not undone by destroying this manager. Only application toplevels are affected; popups and subsurfaces inherit their toplevel's coordinate space. A surface with a committed buffer raises mapped_surface unless it has already been declared self-managed.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Existing surface declarations remain in effect.

request.name: get_keyboard_inset

description.summary: lay the surface out around the on-screen keyboard

request.description:
Create a keyboard inset object for an application toplevel. While it exists the shell no longer moves the surface to keep it clear of the on-screen keyboard; it reports the keyboard's height through the object instead, and the client keeps its content above it.
The request may be sent at any time, with or without a committed buffer, and takes effect immediately rather than on wl_surface.commit. It does not require set_self_managed. A surface has at most one keyboard inset object; another request for it raises keyboard_inset_exists. Destroying this manager does not destroy objects created from it.

interface.name: denial_keyboard_inset_v1

description.summary: on-screen keyboard height for one surface

interface.description:
Reports how much of the surface's bottom edge the on-screen keyboard covers. The surface keeps its configured size: the keyboard does not cause a configure, and the client moves its own content, for example putting a text field directly above the keys and shrinking the area above it.
Only the mobile shell reports a non-zero height. There, application windows reach the bottom of the output, so the keyboard covers the same height of each of them. Elsewhere the height stays zero.
The shell reports each keyboard motion once, when it starts, together with its duration. There is no per-frame traffic: while the user drags the keyboard by hand, the surface is told only where the keyboard settles once released.
Destroying the object returns the surface to the shell's default: it is moved while the keyboard is shown. The object becomes inert when its surface is destroyed. Other compositors need not expose this interface; clients must remain usable without it.

description.summary: stop laying the surface out around the keyboard

event.name: inset
event.description:
The on-screen keyboard covers the bottom height logical pixels of the surface, or will once a motion lasting duration milliseconds ends. Zero height means the keyboard is hidden. Sent once right after the object is created, with the current height and zero duration, then whenever the height changes.
duration is the shell's own motion time; a client animating its layout over it moves in step with the keyboard, and zero means the change is immediate. This event is immediate state: it is not part of a configure sequence and is not applied by wl_surface.commit.
